analysis.summary: Zero-dependency Node.js ESM project. No build step; source runs directly with `node`. The HTTP server reads index.html at startup, listens on PORT (default 3100), and delegates shipping calculations to shipping.mjs. Tests use the built-in Node test runner (node --test). Engine requirement is Node >=22; node:22-bookworm satisfies that. No package installation is needed — there are no dependencies declared in package.json.
analysis.purpose: Shipping Service is a small checkout web application for online shoppers. A shopper enters their order subtotal on a form and instantly sees the delivery charge and final total before paying. Orders under $100 are charged a flat $5 shipping fee; orders of $100 or more ship free. There is no payment system or external service — it is a self-contained quote calculator.
capabilities: View the checkout form in a browser to enter an order subtotal
Get a shipping quote by submitting the form, showing delivery charge and total
Query the quote API directly with GET /quote?subtotal=<amount> for JSON results
Receive a 400 error response for invalid, missing, zero, negative, or out-of-range subtotals
Receive a 404 response for any route other than GET / and GET /quote

languages.name: JavaScript
languages.role: Implements the entire application: the HTTP server (app.mjs), the shipping-fee business logic (shipping.mjs), the unit test suite (tests/quote.test.mjs), and the interactive browser form script embedded in index.html

languages.name: HTML
languages.role: Defines the checkout UI served at GET / — the subtotal input form and output display area

stack: Node.js >=22 (ESM, built-in http, fs/promises, node:test, node:assert)
limitations: No CI configuration file (e.g. .github/workflows) was present in the snapshot, so the runtime choice (node22) is based solely on the engines field in package.json (>=22).
index.html has no separate source file for its inline script — it cannot be linted or tested in isolation without extracting it.
There are no lint, coverage, or integration test scripts defined in package.json beyond the basic node --test suite.
assumptions: The deliberate boundary defect noted in the README is in shipping.mjs: the condition `subtotal > 100` gives free shipping only above $100, but the spec requires free shipping at exactly $100 as well; the correct condition should be `subtotal >= 100`. The existing unit tests do not cover the exact-$100 boundary case, so this defect passes the current test suite.
No package installation step is needed because package.json declares no dependencies (only engines and scripts); npm/pnpm install would be a no-op.
The shell glob `tests/*.test.mjs` is expanded by the Node CLI on Linux and will resolve to tests/quote.test.mjs correctly in the container.

issues.title: Free-shipping boundary at exactly $100
issues.description: When subtotal is exactly 100, the shipping charge is incorrectly calculated as $5 instead of $0. The specification states that orders of $100 or more receive free shipping, including exactly $100. The implementation uses a strict greater-than operator (`>`) instead of greater-than-or-equal (`>=`), causing the boundary value to fall through to the $5 charge.

reproduction.action: GET /quote?subtotal=100.01 (just above boundary — confirmed free shipping)

issues.expected: Status 200 with shipping:0 and total:100 (current code fails this — shipping.mjs uses > instead of >=)
issues.rootCause: In `shipping.mjs` line 5, the condition `subtotal > 100` excludes the boundary value 100 from free shipping. The correct condition per the README spec ('Orders of $100 or more receive free shipping, including exactly $100') is `subtotal >= 100`.
issues.fixExplanation: The single-character change from `>` to `>=` aligns the boundary condition with the documented specification. With `>=`, any subtotal of exactly 100 will produce `shipping: 0` and `total: 100`, matching the expected response. Values above 100 already produce free shipping and are unaffected. Values below 100 continue to produce `shipping: 5`. The existing test suite does not cover the boundary value 100 directly (tests only use 50 and 150), so the defect was not caught by the current tests. A boundary test at subtotal=100 should be added, but per schema rules the test files must not be edited here; that addition is left as a recommendation.
issues.risks: The change is narrowly scoped to one operator in one expression. No other logic paths in `shipping.mjs` or `app.mjs` are touched. The existing passing tests (subtotal=50 → shipping=5; subtotal=150 → shipping=0) remain valid and unaffected. The only observable behavioral change is that subtotal=100 now returns shipping=0 instead of shipping=5. No test in the current suite asserts the old (incorrect) behavior for subtotal=100, so no tests will break. Risk is low.

fixes.explanation: Replace the strict `>` with `>=` in the shipping-tier condition inside `quote()` in `shipping.mjs`. Every other character, line, and CRLF ending is preserved to match the original file exactly.
fixes.risks: Minimal. Only the boundary value 100 changes behavior. All other inputs behave identically to before. No dependency, config, or test file is modified.
